Her research trajectory, developed since the beginning of her doctoral thesis, falls within the area of personalization in intelligent software agents and, more generally, in recommender systems. Specifically, it has focused on techniques and algorithms for learning user preferences to assist them in their tasks.
The research has centered on the use of various Artificial Intelligence techniques (such as Bayesian Networks, Association Rules, and Classification Techniques) to build individual user profiles and, more recently, group profiles, to provide assistance in computer-based tasks performed individually or collaboratively.
This latter topic has been her main focus in recent years, aiming to assist groups as a whole in various domains, including entertainment, social networks, and computer-supported collaborative work.

Online courses Project or software documentation Tutorials The courses folder may be renamed. For example, we can rename it to docs for software/project documentation or tutorials for creating an online course.

Update site menu After renaming or deleting the courses folder, you may wish to update any [[main]] menu links to it by editing your menu configuration at config/_default/menus.toml.
For example, if you delete this folder, you can remove the following from your menu configuration:
[[main]] name = "Courses" url = "courses/" weight = 50 Or, if you are creating a software documentation site, you can rename the courses folder to docs and update the associated Courses menu configuration to:

Hence, if you rename the courses/example/ folder, you should also rename the menu definitions in the front matter of files within courses/example/ from [menu.example] to [menu.<NewFolderName>].

summary:
The main issue faced in this proyect was
the lack of control and traceability over the recycling processes in
a battery factory,
which were managed through printed spreadsheets and manual records.
This methodology not only hindered the tracking of material batches
and their traceability throughout the production process, but also
limited the company’s ability to analyze deviations in production
costs, identify failures by series, and accurately evaluate the
efficiency of the industrial process.


The development of the system aimed to digitalize each stage
of the process, improve the quality of data recording, and enable
the generation of strategic reports to support decision-making.
Likewise, special emphasis was placed on achieving an intuitive
interface for the plant operator, taking into account the specific
usage conditions of the industrial environment.
title: Integrated Management and Traceability System for a Battery Recycling Process

summary:
In an increasingly digital world, the availability of
information has multiplied exponentially. News about urban events—such
as traffic accidents, crimes, or fires—is constantly published in
digital media and on social networks, generating a continuous stream
of data that is difficult for the average user to process
manually. This information overload presents a clear problem:
how can we efficiently and personally access the events that truly
matter, whether due to their geographic proximity or their type?


The system's unique value lies not only in its ability to categorize
news in real time and map it geographically, but also in its scalable
and adaptable design. A modular architecture—based on the separation
of concerns and the use of decoupled components—combined with sound
software engineering practices, allows the solution to evolve easily
and be adapted to other contexts.
title: Geopositioned Visualization and Categorization of News

summary: The use of mobile devices for the study of urban mobility has attracted the attention of the scientific community in the last years. In this work, we address the problem of predicting the user’s next destination given the user’s mobility profile, i.e. her visit history and the set of places she visited during that time. To predict the next visit, our approach relies on a set of predictors, each of which analyzes different aspects of the user’s daily mobility. The output of each predictor consists of a list of places along with the probability of each place being the next destination. The approach combines the output of each predictor into a single one using weights based on the cumulative precision of its previous predictions. Once the user arrives at her destination the proposed approach adapts the set of predictors for future estimations. The predictors in this work were designed so that their training and use have a low computational cost, adapting to the available resources on mobile devices. The experiments carried out over two datasets (Nokia MDC dataset with 52 users and 129,097 visits to 12,869 different places, and a private dataset with 76 users with more than 30 registered days and 47,933 stays) yielded promising results, enhancing performance for 75.8 % of users with an average accuracy of 49.2 % and F1weighted of 42.6 % and an average use of only 48 Megabytes of RAM.
title: Prediction of the next user location using personal tracking data

summary:
The main objective of this project is to define a model based on Machine Learning techniques that can estimate waiting times and predict travel time between two specific points using the public bus system in Tandil. This model will make it possible to recommend the most efficient routes based on a pair of origin and destination coordinates, taking into account a variety of input parameters. It will enable accurate estimations, even considering various factors that affect traffic and vehicle behavior, such as specific hours or days.


The proposed system will not only consider public transport elements like bus lines and routes but also external variables such as the time of day, proximity to the city center, the day of the week, among other relevant factors. Since buses are used daily by a large portion of the population, special emphasis will be placed on using up-to-date and reliable data to provide a service that users can trust.


Through a simple and user-friendly interface, the system will offer a clear view of the public transport status so that users can stay as informed as possible. Regarding system architecture, the goal is to develop a solution accessible on as many mobile devices as possible, regardless of their technical specifications. Likewise, the user interface will be designed to be simple and intuitive, ensuring a pleasant and attractive user experience to encourage adoption by new users.
title: Mobile App for Tracking Bus Locations and Estimating Wait Times

summary:
Visiting a city for the first time is always a challenging experience. Among
the available tourist attractions, travelers must choose and prioritize those that best
match their interests, available time, and budget. As a result, vacation planning often
becomes a stressful activity, and travelers rely on various applications to support
their decision-making process. In this context, tourism recommender systems have emerged
to deal with the information overload that tourists face when visiting a new city. These
systems have focused on different aspects of the domain, such as recommending hotels,
routes, restaurants, itineraries, and attractions.




In this area, group recommender systems have been proposed for users traveling with a
predefined group (e.g., a group of friends or family traveling together). This thesis
consisted in  the design and implementation of a
recommender system in the tourism domain, which leverages mobile devices to recommend
that travelers form groups to visit attractions or points of interest (POIs)
together. This approach utilizes the geolocation capabilities of mobile devices
in two ways. On the one hand, it implicitly learns the user's interests based
on the places they visit, the amount of time spent at each location, and the
time taken to travel to those places. This way, users are not required to manually
log each place they visit or explicitly state their interests, as is required by
most current approaches. On the other hand, it identifies nearby tourists—who also
have the application—and suggests forming a group with those who share similar
interests. Once a group is formed, the system recommends POIs that the entire group
is likely to enjoy.
title: Interest-Based Group Recommender System for Tourism

summary: Product classification is a critical task for the smooth running of the purchase process in e-commerce websites. When it comes to P2P marketplaces, users can act both as sellers and as buyers, and they need to assign predefined categories to the products they want to sell. Besides being tedious for users, this task can result in ambiguous or inaccurate assignments.This article presents a method for the automatic categorization of items offered in a local P2P marketplace using a multi-level classification approach. Our experiments demonstrated a significant improvement in the classification results of the proposed solution compared to a traditional direct classification approach.
title: Automatic classification of products in P2P marketplaces

summary: Data captured by mobile devices enable us, among other things, learn the places where users go, identify their home and workplace, the places they usually visit (e.g., supermarket, gym, etc.), the different paths they take to move from one place to another and even their routines. In summary, with this information, it is possible to learn a user mobility profile. In this work, we propose a lightweight approach for building mobility profiles from data collected with mobile devices. The mobility profiles of a user consist of the places visited, the visit history and the travel paths. Our approach aims to solve some of the challenges and limitations identified in the literature. Particularly, it considers geographic information to identify certain kinds of places, such as open spaces, big places and small places, that are hard to distinguish with existing approaches. We use different sensors and time frequencies to collect data in order to optimize battery consumption and maximize precision. Finally, it executes entirely on the mobile devices, avoiding the exposure of sensitive user information and then preserving user privacy. The proposal was evaluated in the context of the real usage of the developed prototype applications in two cities of Argentina. The results obtained with our approach outperformed other approaches in the literature, both in precision and recall.
title: A Lightweight Approach for Building User Mobility Profiles

summary: Sedentarism is a common problem that can affect human health and wellbeing. Predicting sedentary behaviour is an emerging area that can benefit from data collected from sensors available in ubiquitous devices, such as wearables and smartphones. In this paper, we present an approach aiming at predicting the sedentary behaviour of a user from data collected from sensors installed in wearable/mobile devices. We compare personal and impersonal models using a real-life dataset consisting of sensing data of 48 users during 10 weeks. We found that impersonal models using Deep Neural Networks were able to accurately predict the subject's future sedentary behaviour.
title: Predicting future sedentary behaviour using wearable and mobile devices

summary:
En el siguiente artículo se describe la experiencia conjunta realizada para el desarrollo
de un prototipo de asistente inteligente que acercará a vendedores y compradores en un portal de ventas
online. Originalmente el proyecto buscaba realizar una caracterización inteligente del usuario con sus
preferencias a corto plazo y las características geoespaciales que lo definan. El proyecto buscó brindar
alertas inteligentes sobre artículos de potencial interés para los usuarios, siempre considerando que es
crucial que la información sea adquirida de una forma no intrusiva e inteligente. Con la sinergia alcanzada
entre las partes a partir del desarrollo conjunto de actividades, se fueron apreciando muchas ventanas de
oportunidades que surgieron con el conocimiento del análisis del portal por parte de los investigadores,
y con el conocimiento de las técnicas de Inteligencia Artificial por parte de la empresa. Durante el
trabajo realizado en conjunto se fueron adaptando los distintos objetivos a fin de poder abarcar las
necesidades efectivas de la empresa, logrando una colaboración exitosa entre las partes.
title: Un caso de éxito en la colaboración entre empresa e institutos de investigación para la recomendación inteligente de anuncios en un portal de venta online

content:
The spread of disinformation and hate speech on social media via the Internet has become a critical global issue. In recent years, there has been a notable increase in both the dissemination of fake news, rumors, deception, and other forms of disinformation, as well as the use of abusive language, incitement to violence, harassment, and other types of hate speech. Both aspects contribute to what is known as “online harm,” which can have potentially severe consequences for individuals and society, ranging from public health issues to the disruption of democratic systems.
This project focuses on defining new algorithms and recommendation systems aimed at mitigating the negative effects of harmful online content. The main objectives of this project are:
Defining new methods for learning user profiles that model their preferences and behavior regarding malicious content by analyzing heterogeneous information from social media platforms. Defining and categorizing users based on their role in the spread of online harm. Designing novel harm-aware recommendation system approaches that incorporate mechanisms to counteract the effects of harmful content in social networks.
summary: This project focuses on defining new algorithms and recommendation systems aimed at mitigating the negative effects of harmful online content.
title: Online Harm-Aware Recommendation Systems in Social Networks

summary:
The main goal of HelpMePublish is to provide support in the task of selecting the most appropriate journal for individuals interested in publishing a scientific article.


To achieve this goal, the development of a multi-publisher journal search and recommendation system is proposed. Based on information from a scientific article (title, keywords, abstract, etc.), the system will suggest scientific journals in which the article’s content is relevant to the journal’s scope.


Using the information provided by the user, the system searches and compares against a database containing information about journals and publishers. It will then suggest the options that best match the provided characteristics.


The proposed approach will be implemented as a web platform that allows users to easily search for journals based on different criteria. Additionally, the system will offer an interface that facilitates the comparison between various journals to assist in the selection process.


The quality of the recommendation system will be evaluated from two perspectives. The first, called the Automatic Perspective, will use already published articles and analyze whether the recommended journal matches the one in which the article was actually published. The second perspective focuses on the user. In this case, the end users will be researchers from the Computing and Systems area at UNICEN. The aim is to compare the recommendations from this approach with those obtained from existing publisher-specific search tools. Specifically, the researchers will assess the quality of the recommendations based on various qualitative aspects.
title: HelpMePublish - A Support Tool for Selecting Scientific Journals

summary:
The problem of predicting future sedentary behavior has previously been addressed by analyzing only the inactive/stationary time of a subject, and the performance of various models has been measured and compared. Alternatively, this thesis defines Future Sedentary Behavior Prediction (FSBP) as the task of predicting whether a user's physical activity will, on average, exceed 1.5 METs in the near future. Although MET is a standard metric in the health field for measuring activity intensity in terms of energy expenditure, its use for predicting sedentary behavior through wearable and mobile devices remains unexplored.


In this work, an approach is presented for predicting a subject’s future sedentary behavior in terms of their MET level, using various Deep Learning models. The prediction is based on the observation of values obtained from multiple sensors on wearable and mobile devices.
title: Sedentary Behavior Prediction Based on Lifelogging Data Analysis

summary:
The main objective of this final project was to design and develop a software system capable of predicting the time it would take a person to travel from one specific location to another using the public bus transportation system in the city of Tandil. Additionally, a mechanism was developed to identify the most recommended possible routes between a pair of origin and destination coordinates, based on certain input parameters, aiming to produce reliable results regardless of the many factors that affect vehicle movement.


The proposed system therefore considered not only aspects related to public transportation—such as bus line and route—but also external factors such as time of day, city center traffic, day of the week, and other conditions.


Given the high daily demand for public buses by citizens, the system sought to use the most recent and accurate information available to provide a service that users could trust. With the collected data and the use of various graphs and diagrams, it was possible to gain a clearer and more precise understanding of the performance of the transportation system.


Additionally, the implementation of a series of metrics allowed for a mathematical analysis of the performance of the proposed models.


During development, special attention was given to ensuring that the data used by both the model and the application did not compromise the privacy of public transport employees, passengers, or any other individuals. Likewise, no information regarding bus infrastructure was stored or disclosed, thus guaranteeing a fully secure and trustworthy system.


At the system architecture level, the goal was to create a structure that was compatible with the widest possible range of mobile devices, regardless of their technological specifications. Furthermore, a simple and user-friendly interface was designed to ensure that the user experience was intuitive, appealing, and pleasant, while also encouraging new users to adopt the application.
title: Mobile Application for Navigation and Time Estimation in Public Bus Transportation

summary:
Social networks are usually used by citizens to report or complain about traffic
incidents that affect their daily mobility. Automatically finding traffic-related reports and
extracting useful information from them is not a trivial task, due to the informal language used
in social networks, to the lack of geographic metadata, and to the large amount of non traffic-related
publications. In this article, we address this problem by combining Machine Learning and Natural
Language Processing techniques. Our approach (a) filters publications that report traffic incidents
in social networks, (b) extracts geographic information from the textual content of the publications,
and (c) provides a broadcasting service that clusters all the reports of the same incident. We compared
the performance of our approach with state of the art approaches and with a popular traffic-specific
social network, obtaining promising results.
title: Mining Social Networks to Detect Traffic Incidents

summary:
The objective of this project was to develop an application for Android mobile phones capable of identifying a user's relevant locations based on the traces left during their daily mobility. In addition, the application was able to recognize when the user returned to a previously visited location.


For the development of the application, the aim was to find a solution that would be both as accurate and efficient as possible. To achieve this, the goal was to accurately detect the time the user spent at a specific location while minimizing mobile battery consumption. To this end, an algorithm was proposed that used WiFi network sensors, as they offer the best balance between accuracy and battery usage.




The learning algorithm was defined as performing the task of taking, as input, a s|equence of records obtained from the mobile device's WiFi sensor and, based on them, producing a list of the places visited by the device. A specific sequence of records collected during a visit was used to define a waypoint  for the location—essentially the “signature” stored for that place. This signature was then compared with other signatures obtained from subsequent visits to the same or different places. On the other hand, the recognition algorithm used the various waypoints learned during the previous stage—one for each location—to detect when the device returned to any of those places.




Once the application development was completed, an evaluation was carried out to validate the efficiency and effectiveness of the proposed solution. During the evaluation, the application was installed on the mobile devices of a selected group of individuals with different daily routines, in order to ensure a good variety of visited locations. The volunteers were asked to record their entry and exit times for each place visited in a logbook. At the end of the experiment, the places detected by the developed application were compared against the ground truth obtained from the users’ manual entries.
title: Detection of Places Visited by the User Based on WiFi Access Points Recorded by Their Mobile Devices

summary:
The general objective of this research is to examine whether the exchange rate of Bitcoin reflects people's opinions about the digital currency. To explore this, it is important to establish whether previous research has shown that investors are influenced by sentiment regarding other traditional investments, such as stocks. It is also relevant to examine the characteristics of investments that are more susceptible to public commentary, and whether those same characteristics apply to Bitcoin. Furthermore, since this paper uses publicly available data from the internet, it is important to assess the reliability of that source and where it has been previously used, particularly in relation to financial markets.


The proposal of this work consists in the development of approaches for predicting currency trends, for which Machine Learning techniques will be applied, as they offer the ability to learn from data and allow the software to evolve automatically.


This proposal is based on the general objective of the project, which is to develop a tool that provides the necessary support to make informed speculations about monetary trends, using Bitcoin as a case study.


The tool to be developed will use trust metrics from the analyzed posts, taking into account user characteristics (such as whether the account is verified, number of followers, geographic location, etc.) and characteristics of the post itself (keywords, sentiment analysis, whether the comment is positive or negative, etc.).


After the analysis is performed, each post (a tweet) will be assigned a score to support the speculation of the trend.
title: Bitcoin Value Trend Detection Approach Based on the Observation of Social Media Impact

summary:
Managing parking spaces is one of the major challenges in urban
mobility. The use of restricted hours or metered parking are the
traditional ways in which municipalities have addressed this
issue. However, finding a parking spot is becoming an increasingly
difficult problem due to the continuous growth of the vehicle
fleet.




In addition to drivers having to spend their time searching for
parking, at least three negative side effects are generated:


1. Air pollution, which harms the environment,


2. Noise pollution, which bothers and affects citizens, and


3. Traffic congestion, which impacts traffic flow and causes
frustration among drivers.




The development of new technologies such as the Internet of
Things, mobile devices, and smart parking meters is providing
new tools to offer more services to citizens and to allow
for more detailed control over the use of parking spaces.




Most existing works addressing the parking problem analyze
it in the context of large cities, using various expensive
devices, or by allowing users to participate in the collection
of data that will later be used to provide possible solutions. This
becomes even more difficult to implement in medium or small cities,
where budget constraints are common, and the relatively small
number of users can only provide a limited amount of data.




This work proposes the development of a smart parking solution
primarily based on data obtained from the parking meters of the
city of Tandil, a city where no solution to this problem has
yet been implemented.
title: Smart Assistant for Parking in Urban Areas

content:
Crowdsensing or mobile crowdsensing is a technique that uses mobile devices to efficiently collect data and enables the development of numerous large-scale applications.
Human participation is one of its most important features, and human mobility offers unprecedented opportunities for both data collection and transmission.
The collected data is then used to extract information that allows for measuring, mapping, visualizing, estimating, or inferring any process of common interest.
This technique is particularly useful for addressing issues related to urban mobility, one of the major challenges cities face today.
In this context, the project tackles various urban mobility problems from the perspective of crowdsensing.
In short, it aims to generate value-added information from data sensed about the individual mobility of citizens, with the goal of improving collective mobility.
summary: This project aims to generate value-added information from data sensed about the individual mobility of citizens, with the goal of improving collective mobility.
title: Intelligent urban mobility through crowdsensing

summary:
Conformance between architecture and implementation is a key aspect of
architecture-centric development. However, the architecture as documented and the architecture
as implemented tend to diverge from each other over time. Thus, conformance checks should be
run periodically on the system in order to detect and correct differences. Despite having a
structural conformance analysis, assessing whether the main scenarios describing the architectural
behavior are faithfully implemented in the code is still challenging. Checking conformance
to architectural scenarios is usually a time-consuming and error-prone activity. In this article,
we describe ArchLearner, a tool to assist architects to bridge the gap between architecture and
its implementation. The architecture is specified with Use-Case Maps (UCMs), a notation for modeling
both high-level structure and behavior. ArchLearner uses Markov Models to detect code deviations
with respect to predetermined UCMs, based on the analysis of system execution traces for
those UCMs. The results from two case-studies have shown that ArchLearner is practical and
reduces conformance checking efforts.
title: A Variable Order Markov Model for Architecture Conformance Checking

content:
The project aims to develop a prototype that connects buyers and sellers through an intelligent characterization of each user, considering their short-term preferences and defining geospatial characteristics. This approach enables smart alerts about items of interest within nearby geographic areas.
A key focus of the project is ensuring easy adoption by acquiring user knowledge in a non-intrusive way using pre-existing information. Additionally, it emphasizes deducing the geolocation of product and service listings, which is particularly important for individual users who are often reluctant to share such information.
summary: The project aims to develop a prototype that connects buyers and sellers through an intelligent characterization of each user, considering their short-term preferences and defining geospatial characteristics.
title: Intelligent Advertisement Recommendation for an Online Sales Platform Based on Implicit User Preference Acquisition and Geospatial Conditions

content:
The spread of any infectious disease, such as COVID-19, which currently affects us, mainly occurs through the transmission of an infectious agent via individual mobility. Therefore, knowing the places where an infected individual has traveled and stayed is of utmost importance to analyze which other individuals or groups may have been exposed to contagion and to develop strategies and optimize available resources.
Crowdsensing, or mobile crowdsensing, is a technique that uses a group of individuals with mobile devices capable of sensing and/or collectively computing data to extract information that allows measuring, mapping, visualizing, estimating, or inferring any process of common interest. This technique falls within the paradigms of geo-crowdsourcing and Volunteered Geographic Information (VGI).
The general objective of this project is to utilize crowdsensing techniques to design and develop a digital platform that can aid decision-making in the management of the COVID-19 pandemic.
The proposed digital platform focuses on the use of mobile devices by citizens. Modern mobile devices are equipped with sensors that allow them to record and infer various aspects of the user’s context, including their geographic location. A mobile device can determine its location not only through GPS but also via nearby WiFi access points in a process called WiFi Positioning Systems (WPS). This process consists of triangulating the device’s location based on the positions of nearby WiFi access points. While GPS-based location tracking works best outdoors and in open spaces, WPS-based location tracking is more effective indoors, where there are more WiFi access points available for triangulation.
By appropriately utilizing both localization mechanisms, it is possible to determine a user’s location almost anywhere and at any time. Additionally, using other device sensors, such as the accelerometer, it is possible to detect whether the device is in motion or stationary. This allows for adjusting the frequency of location tracking (for example, it is unnecessary to track the device when it is stationary), thus reducing GPS/WPS usage and minimizing battery consumption.
The proposed project is built upon a prototype mobile application developed by the research team, aimed at non-intrusively recording a user’s physical activity and geographic location throughout their daily routine. Based on this data, the app detects the places visited by the user and the paths taken to move from one place to another. The information collected by the application on various citizens’ mobile devices would form the foundation of the proposed digital platform, which would enable the analysis and control of a pandemic like COVID-19, where citizen mobility is a key factor.
The application could not only provide information about citizen mobility but also establish communication channels with users (either a general information channel or a specific channel for an individual) and allow citizens to actively generate useful data or information through reports.
summary: The objective of the project is to develop a platform that supports a georeferenced social network for the epidemiological tracking of the COVID-19 pandemic.
title: Analysis and Traceability of the Spread of the COVID-19 Virus Through Mobile Devices

summary:
Collaboration is essential for individuals working in groups to achieve a common
goal. The understanding of the collaborative profile of each member of a team is extremely
useful to understand and predict his/her performance in future teamwork. Users can demonstrate
their collaborative skills on many digital platforms. Among them, video games enable
to capture the players’ behavior by the direct observation of their actions, while
engaging them in a pleasant activity. In this work, we propose an approach for building
collaborative profiles of a group of people working together towards a common goal, using
an online game as a shared environment and a well-known theory about groups’
dynamics: SYMLOG. This profile can be useful to know which features each member
should train to improve his/her collaborative skills and to predict the performance
of the group. We validate our approach with 98 players to evaluate the similarity between
the profiles generated by our approach and the profiles derived from the SYMLOG
questionnaire, which is the usual tool used with this theory
title: Building SYMLOG profiles with an online collaborative game

summary:
The proposal of this work consists in the development of approaches for inferring team roles based on a classification derived from Belbin's Team Roles, using machine learning techniques—a branch of Artificial Intelligence.




This proposal is aligned with the general objective of the project, which is to develop a tool that assists in the detection of roles. Additionally, through the analysis of each student’s behavior based on Belbin’s theory, the tool will enable the automatic formation of efficient groups.




The chosen collaborative work environment for developing this project involves various applications within the Google platform. These include Hangouts, a communication tool that users will use to interact and discuss the tasks at hand, and Google Docs, a word processor that allows multiple users to work simultaneously, fostering online collaboration.




On one hand, data will be collected from various group chat sessions through conversation analysis. On the other hand, prior to engaging in collaborative work, users will complete surveys based on the SYMLOG model of group analysis. This model proposes a classification of key personality factors that impact group performance and provides tools for measuring them. The results reveal the presence of traits relevant to group dynamics, which can be directly linked to Belbin’s Team Roles. This relationship will offer an initial view of the roles as self-perceived by the users.




All the collected information will be analyzed using artificial intelligence techniques, applying strategies to develop an approach that can efficiently classify user roles.
title: Intelligent Assistance for Inferring User Roles in Computer-Supported Collaborative Work

summary:
The proposal made in this thesis consisted of the development of a framework to facilitate the generation of collaborative user profiles, following the SYMLOG model, based on their interactions within a given shared space. This profile generation was carried out using deep learning techniques, specifically through the application of various concepts inherent to neural networks. Several neural network concepts were experimented with, which were then integrated into a single model in order to maximize the accuracy of the generated profiles.




To validate the generated profiles, four deep learning approaches were evaluated, each varying in the concepts they employed. The first approach primarily used dense layers in the neural network architecture; the second utilized convolutional layers; and the third relied on recurrent operations. Finally, the fourth approach combined the best aspects of these concepts to create a hybrid neural network architecture that improved upon the metrics achieved by the previous approaches.




In addition to the framework, a web application was implemented to graphically organize the information obtained. In this way, the use of such tools was made more accessible to users with minimal knowledge of these types of systems. Since the framework was designed to function as a backend, the information it provided was displayed on the client side through various graphs and tables. This approach facilitated understanding, avoiding the need to interpret formats such as JSON or CSV.




The process of building collaborative profiles began with a set of messages from the dialogue generated by group members working collaboratively to solve a common task. These messages were processed by the neural network models to categorize each one of them according to the IPA method. Based on these categories, correspondences were established between the IPA method and SYMLOG. That is, a mapping was performed from the categorizations obtained by the networks to the corresponding trinomial of each dimension in the SYMLOG model.
title: Framework for Building Collaborative User Profiles with Deep Learning Techniques Based on Big Data

summary:
This work aimed to develop a tool that assisted and facilitated the task of individuals working with collaborative groups by assigning them various tasks to solve. The group members interacted using online chat tools to address the given problem. The tool developed in this thesis was expected to help detect collaborative behaviors and conflicts described by Bales in workgroups. Based on the profiles generated for each individual, it enabled the formation of workgroups in which the likelihood of collaborative conflicts was minimized.




This work proposed various classification approaches to analyze interactions in collaborative tasks and to classify the free-form text obtained from the chat on the collaborative platform into one of the IPA categories. An approach was evaluated in the classroom context, achieving significant improvements over previous methods. Based on the classification of interactions into IPA categories, alerts were triggered when the percentage of a group's interactions fell outside the ranges proposed by Bales.




In addition, the solution proposed in this thesis created individual profiles and offered the option to generate new workgroups using the generated profiles, aiming to form groups with a low probability of collaborative conflict.
title: Intelligent Team Formation Tool for Conflict Reduction in Computer-Supported Collaborative Work

summary:
Defining an argument as invalid is often easier than explaining why it is invalid—and even when an argument is refuted, the reasoning behind the refutation is often not sufficiently strong.




The main objective of this work is to develop an approach that, given an argumentative sentence expressed in natural language, can identify the flaws that render it invalid. This approach will provide the necessary support to detect argumentative errors in large volumes of data efficiently and with good performance.




To deepen the analysis, a semantic study of argumentative sentences will be carried out. Integrating semantics with syntax is not a trivial task, as it requires adapting 'common sense' for machines.




To conduct this study, a Knowledge Discovery in Databases (KDD) process is proposed, implementing each of its stages.




Ultimately, two tools will be developed with the goal of classifying sentences by detecting errors in their construction. To achieve this classification, various algorithms will be used to determine which one has the highest accuracy rate.
title: An Approach for the Automatic Detection of Flaws in Argument Construction

summary:
In this article, we propose an approach to market basket analysis
based on the notion of social influence. While traditional market basket analysis
looks for combinations of products that frequently co-occur in transactions, we
seek to find a set of influential products that, if bought by a customer, will
increase the sales volume of the shop. We believe that customers who purchase
influential products would also be influenced to purchase other products. We
validated our approach with two real-world datasets collected from online shoppings
and one dataset collected from a supermarket concluding that influential products
identified by our approach increase the influence spread with respect to different
baselines: best-selling, highest centrality, frequent sequence initiator, and
most promoted products.
title: Influence-based approach to market basket analysis

summary:
Sentiment identification in text is a significant field of study (opinion mining – sentiment analysis), with social media platforms like Twitter attracting the interest of researchers in language processing as well as in political and social sciences. The task typically involves detecting whether a text expresses a positive, negative, or neutral sentiment. Sentiment can be general or directed toward a specific topic, such as a person, a product, or an event.




In this context, we present  a web application that interacts with Twitter and is intended for a wide range of users, as it can be used both for recreational and entertainment purposes, as well as to analyze social media responses to a product or service from a particular company or organization.




This application allows users to collect tweets based on different search criteria: keyword (hashtag), replies to a given tweet, or tweets from a specific user. It then provides the ability to analyze the sentiment of this set of opinions using various algorithms:


* **Machine Learning**: The application includes an algorithm that has been trained on an extensive dataset of tweets labeled as positive, negative, or neutral.


* **Grammatical Structures**: The underlying technology of this algorithm is based on a new type of recursive neural network that relies on grammatical structures. It is the only model capable of accurately capturing the effects of negation and its scope within positive and negative phrases.




Finally, the application presents a graphical and interactive framework where users can navigate through the data and perform a detailed analysis of the information obtained. This was implemented using a Business Intelligence tool.
title: Comprehensive Tool for Sentiment Analysis on Social Media

summary:
When checking students´ source codes, teachers tend to overlook some errors. This work
introduces Soploon, a tool that automatically detects novice programmer errors. By using this tool,
teachers can reduce the number of overlooked errors. Thus, students receive a more complete and
exhaustive feedback about their errors and misconceptions.
title: Soploon: A virtual assistant to help teachers to detect object-oriented errors in students’ source codes

summary:
The analysis of group dynamics is extremely useful for understanding and
predicting the performance of teamworks, since in this context, collaboration
problems can naturally arise. Artificial intelligence, and specially machine learning
techniques, enables automating the observation process and the analysis of groups of
users who use an online collaborative platform. Among the online collaborative platforms
available, games are an attractive alternative for all audiences that enable capturing
the players' behavior by observing their social interactions, while engaging them in
a pleasant activity. In this paper, we present experimental results of classifying
observed conversations in an online game to collaborative behaviors, guided by the
Interaction Process Analysis, a theory for categorizing social interactions. The proposed
automation of the classification process can be used to assist teachers or team leaders
to detect alterations in the balance of group reactions and to improve their performance
by indicating actions to improve the balance.
title: De  'discusión táctica'  en  juego de colaboración a 'conductas': enfoque de clasificación en etapas

summary:
In a computer-supported collaborative work (CSCW) environment,
a group of people can work together to fulfill a given assignment. In this
context, collaborative problems might naturally arise. The detection of these
problems is extremely important for teachers or team leaders to help the
team members to improve their collaborative skills and the resolution of
the collaboration problems. The observation and analysis of the interaction
process of several groups is a time-consuming and difficult task for any
teacher or team leader. In this article, we propose a multi-phase
classification approach to automatically classify free text observed
form the chat of a CSCW environment into different collaborative
categories of behavior. We obtained promising results that can be
used to help teachers or team leaders with the interaction process
analysis in order to focus only in the resolution?s actions of the problems
that might arise.
title: Classification of collaborative behavior from free text interactions

summary:
User modeling is an important area in the field of artificial
intelligence. Traditionally, user modeling approaches have focused on individual
features of users, leaving aside aspects of users as part of a group. However,
in enterprise, academic, or political contexts, it is common to find groups of
people working together to solve a collaborative task using online collaborative
platforms. In this context, counting with a knowledge based on describing
the users' behavior when working in a group (i.e., the collaborative profile)
is vital for a system aiming at assisting them to enhance their collaborative
abilities that might impact the group dynamics. Traditionally, collaborative
abilities have been measured by means of questionnaires or by an external human
observer. In this work, we propose an approach to build collaborative profiles
by the means of observation of users' behavior in a collaborative serious game. The
main advantage of our approach is that it avoids external human observers of the
group dynamics and the use of self-perception questionnaires. We obtained promising
results when comparing the user profiles obtained with our approach with respect to
the classical measurement instruments.
title: Modeling Users' Collaborative Behavior With a Serious Game

content:
Platforms for binary options trading and long-term stock trading are abundant in the market. However, there is no intelligent adjustment operation for binary options based on a community model of users grouped under social network models. Similarly, there are no platforms on the market with bots for short-term volatility placement or user grouping to analyze behavior using social graph methods.
This project aims to develop a prototype algorithm to analyze the specific market conditions of binary options and trading based on the concept of short-term volatility. In both cases, the algorithm will be capable of predicting how to invest efficiently within an active and identified community.
summary: This project aims to develop a prototype algorithm to analyze the specific market conditions of binary options and trading based on the concept of short-term volatility.
title: Recommender System for Decision-Making in Binary Options Trading

content:
Recommendation systems are valuable tools for reducing the information overload that users face when searching for and analyzing data. Consequently, they are increasingly used in the software development market to add value to applications. A recommendation system (RS) can be seen as an intelligent agent that assists a user in filtering items within a certain domain, using various techniques (e.g., user profiles, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning) to identify the items that best match the user’s preferences or needs.
Many RS applications have gained popularity due to the rise of social media platforms and the widespread use of mobile devices. Traditionally, RSs have focused on individual users by analyzing their preference profiles, browsing history, or past searches. In recent years, researchers have started to consider that RS users can also be groups of users, which has led to the development of group recommendation systems (GRS), the central focus of this project.
Naturally, GRS techniques are based on extensions of techniques used for individual recommendation systems (IRS). However, a key aspect of a GRS (which goes beyond an IRS) is group decision-making (or social choice), which involves making recommendations that satisfy the group as a whole while addressing potential conflicts among members’ interests.
From a software development perspective, it is common practice to start with a solution conceived as an IRS, and later, due to client or business requirements, extend it to group contexts, many of which involve social networks. This presents challenges both in terms of the functionalities to be incorporated into the original IRS and the design decisions required to incrementally build the new GRS from existing software assets.
These new functionalities and design decisions affect the quality attributes of the GRS solution, such as performance, information privacy, and distribution, among others. In this context, the project addresses the challenges related to the functional aspects of a GRS (built from one or more IRS) and the software design process for these systems. To achieve this, a multi-agent modeling approach is proposed, applying negotiation mechanisms to achieve balanced recommendations in the GRS.
The project will explore techniques and architectures for designing and developing GRS applications that enable the reuse of software assets and the analysis of emerging quality attributes of such applications. This combination is both novel and valuable for the software industry. The research aims to advance the state of the art in GRS construction and provide engineering guidelines and models for developing applications with GRS capabilities.
summary:
The project explore techniques and architectures for designing and developing
GRS applications that enable the reuse of software assets and the analysis of emerging
quality attributes of such applications.
title: Design and Development of Group Recommendation Systems with a Multi-Agent Approach

summary:
The objective of this work was to study learning techniques—specifically supervised learning—for the prediction of non-existent or hidden links between users within the same social network.




Networks could be represented as graphs, in which the nodes corresponded to users and the edges to the relationships between them. From the perspective of supervised learning, it was necessary to create datasets containing all the information from the graphs. The instances of these datasets corresponded to each pair of nodes, and the attributes to the similarity values between them, based on various functions. The class of the instances was determined by the presence or absence of a link between the nodes; therefore, link prediction became a binary classification problem.




The Gephi tool was used as a foundation for implementing the necessary requirements to conduct the experiments. It provided utilities for graph manipulation and for calculating various similarity functions between pairs of nodes. Additionally, new functionalities were added for dataset creation and classification from graphs, as well as a set of techniques to enhance and make the classification process more flexible: instance filtering, feature selection, and dataset balancing.




Four networks with very different characteristics were used for the experiments, varying in both size and intrinsic structure. Three of the networks ranged from small to medium in size, while the fourth and most important one corresponded to a crawl of a portion of Twitter and was therefore significantly larger. It was also the most disconnected network of the four.




Due to the vast number of possible combinations of networks, techniques, and classifiers to be tested, the experimentation was carried out in stages. Since individual similarity functions were useful on their own for link prediction, though with very different behaviors, the objective of the final stage was to compare the supervised learning approach against these functions, evaluating the quality of both types of predictive models.




Various conclusions were reached. Instance filtering based on common neighbors improved classification in all cases. Feature selection proved beneficial for small and medium-sized networks. Dataset balancing was particularly useful for the Twitter dataset, where extreme imbalance had previously prevented significantly meaningful classifications. Finally, the learning-based approach provided greater quality and flexibility than individual functions; however, it required more extensive testing and configuration. In large networks, function-based approaches became ineffective due to their low flexibility and performance.
title: Link Prediction in Social Networks Using a Learning-Based Approach

summary:
Automatic classification of music is a complex and interesting research
problem due to the difficulties that arise when determining the musical features
that should be considered for classification and the characteristics that define
each particular genre. In this article, we propose an approach for automatic genre
classification of symbolic music pieces. We evaluated our approach with a dataset
consisting of 225 pieces using a taxonomy of three genres and nine subgenres. Results
demonstrate that by only extracting a small set of features from the MIDI files, we
are able to obtain better results than competing approaches that use one hundred
features for classification.
title: Genre classification of symbolic pieces of music
